text:
The Belmont Stakes features a number of impressive horses though one stands out above the rest(Image: Will Waldron/Albany Times Union via Getty Images)

The Belmont Stakes represents the final jewel of the Triple Crown, and despite being one of horse racing's premier events, a tragedy later that day cast a shadow over the weekend three years ago.

In June 2023, Excursionniste was navigating the far turn in a race following the main event when it sustained what was described as a "catastrophic injury to its left front leg," according to a statement released by the New York Racing Association (NYRA). This marked yet another fatality in what had been a year plagued by them in the sport.

As the horse racing world moves forward, there remains a sobering reality that a horse can perish at any time. This grim reminder resurfaces as the latest edition of the prestigious race commences in New York.

Following Excursionniste's injury, it was euthanized, prompting Little Blue Bird Stables to share a brief statement on social media after the decision was made. "Devestated. There's just no other word," the statement began at the time, per ESPN.

"He was our big, goofy, talented, crazy, 1 for 16 NYB superstar. We do everything as a team, and will console as one for quite a while."

Excursionniste became the third horse to perish that year and highlighted a more troubling picture of annual racehorse fatalities. Notably, 12 horses died at Churchill Downs that year, resulting in races being suspended due to the numerous horse deaths at the venue.

Horse fatalities also occurred during Preakness Stakes weekend, further highlighting how the three premier events on the horse racing calendar had been overshadowed by deaths.

ESPN also reported that horse racing fatalities in 2023 saw a slight uptick compared to the previous year, rising to 1.32 deaths per 1,000 starts, up from 1.25 per 1,000. These figures are based on data gathered by the Horse Racing Integrity and Safety Authority.

Following Excursionniste's death, the NYRA issued a statement reaffirming its commitment to horse safety.

Despite how horse racing as evolved over the years, it is still a dangerous one for those involved(Image: Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images)

"NYRA prioritizes safety and integrity above all other considerations and continuously evaluates all aspects of the operation to provide the safest possible environment for training and racing," their statement read at the time. "NYRA will closely review the circumstances around this incident."

The Belmont Stakes' veterinary team also put out a statement following the horse's injury and the subsequent decision to euthanize him.

The statement read: "Despite the immediate response and best efforts of on-site attending veterinarians, the horse was humanely euthanized due to the severity of the injury."

People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals, better known as PETA, issued a strongly-worded statement after the incident, alleging that the organization had sought to conduct CT scans on horses to identify any pre-existing injuries but was turned down. "Racing couldn't manage to keep all horses alive for even one Triple Crown day this year," PETA senior vice president Kathy Guillermo said in a statement to The Associated Press. "They refused. The racing industry is digging its own grave - as well as this horse's."
